stage: B -- repair of references the restructure made stale
rule: Only paths, module names and imports were changed. No model logic, experiment setting, seed, metric or number was touched. Every entry was found by resolving the reference, not by reading the file name.

asset_locations.why: the checkpoint and the LA prior are shipped at assets/generator/; the old path resolved to nothing, so GENERATOR_CKPT and LOGPI_LA were both unreachable
the purity label sets are shipped at assets/rulers/; every purity scoring resolved a missing file
the v8 lineage ruler was addressed by four scripts through a hard-coded old path; they now share one constant
the archived CellTypist histograms are shipped at assets/rulers/celltypist/
same move, addressed through the config constants so there is one authority
provenance string in the audit output; it named a path that does not exist in this repository
the frozen distance rulers moved with the analysis package; load_frozen() could not find any of them

asset_locations.from: DATA = ROOT / "data"; MODELS = ROOT / "assets" / "models"; REFERENCES = ROOT / "assets" / "references"
asset_locations.to: ASSETS = ROOT / "assets" / "toy"; DATA = ASSETS / "data"; MODELS = ASSETS / "frozen" / "models"; REFERENCES = ASSETS / "frozen" / "references"
asset_locations.why: the toy assets are shipped under assets/toy/; toy2d.chain could not load the network, the tilts, the discriminators or the reference draws
recorded provenance path; the pre-registration is shipped under docs/prereg/
the CFGen sampler is shipped under baselines/cfgen/code/

module_names.why: the module was renamed; run_one, the single sampling entry point, failed at import

module_names.from: from crndiff import model_conditional as MC
module_names.to: from crndiff import conditional_model as MC

module_names.from: from crndiff import model_masked_mdlm as MD
module_names.to: from baselines.mdlm import model_masked_mdlm as MD
module_names.why: the MDLM port moved into baselines/mdlm/ with the other baselines

module_names.to: from crndiff import config as C
module_names.why: the relative import pointed at the package it left; baselines/__init__.py and baselines/mdlm/__init__.py were added so the module is importable where it now lives
the sidecar records the sha256 of the script it inherits from; the old name raised FileNotFoundError
ten subprocess invocations still named the retired tools package and its ticket-numbered modules
the tilt-table builder writes next to its own module, which now lives in scripts/
the usage line named the retired module
the error told the reader to run a module that no longer exists

added_because_something_referenced_them.why: run_ours_downstream_chain.py runs it as a subprocess for every training seed; it had not been copied
edits: the docstring header and usage line name the new path
the --x-root default was an absolute path on the author machine; it is now assets/legacy_root, which is the same tree

added_because_something_referenced_them.why: run_ours_downstream_chain.py runs it as a subprocess to export each fitted discriminator; it had not been copied
the archived e33 body loads it on every downstream run; without it evaluation/downstream_multiseed.py stops at load_manifest()

other.why: the guard hashes evaluation/score_purity.py, whose bytes moved when the module was renamed (hvg -> crndiff, analysis -> evaluation) and its comments were translated. The scoring code itself is unchanged; the old digest is recorded in the comment above the constant
every array path in the archived manifest is an absolute Windows path under the old HVG2K tree, which is mirrored here as archive/. The arrays themselves (about 7.6 GB) are not shipped

other.to: writes out/toy/figdata.npz and compares its sha256 against the shipped copy
other.why: a rebuild overwrote a shipped artefact. The rebuild is bitwise identical (89952d0f7da4b6e493ea54d3ac93dc831f275f40a018547907d6f72ed05bdd91), and results/ is now read-only to this script

other.from: the H0 gate description was the original Chinese ticket text
other.why: nothing reads this field; it is documentation

stage_c_public_release.what: A second pass, driven by a clean-clone smoke test: the repository was exported through a git index into an empty directory, installed into a fresh virtual environment from requirements.txt alone, and every documented command was run there.

found_and_fixed.why: the unanchored rule also matched archive/universality_fk/out/, so four archived artefacts the scorers read -- E30plus_manifest.json, E30plus_full_metrics.json, E33_downstream.json and E33_prereg.json -- would never have been committed. Verified with git check-ignore

git line-ending normalisation would have rewritten the frozen modules on checkout and broken every sha256 guard. Two sha-asserted files (crndiff/frozen/fk_hvg_v2.py, evaluation/frozen/e30plus_eval_cpu_worker.py) are stored with CRLF, so this is not hypothetical
the six driver paths for the scVI and scANVI baselines still pointed into the retired tree; the drivers are shipped under baselines/
recorded ruler path in the scoring output named a directory that no longer exists
the default output directory was inside the code tree

found_and_fixed.to: exit 1 only on a MISMATCH; --strict restores the old behaviour
found_and_fixed.why: a fresh clone is missing the large arrays by design, so the old exit code made the first command in the README look like a failure and could not be used in CI

found_and_fixed.to: MIT for the code, CC-BY-4.0 noted for the redistributed panel arrays
found_and_fixed.why: a public repository without a licence cannot legally be used or reproduced

added.why: one command that runs all fifteen offline entry points and compares the rebuilt toy figure extract against the shipped copy by sha256
runs check_assets, the smoke test and compileall on push, on Python 3.10 and 3.12
acceptance gates G2 and G3 name them as their archived references; only the .npy had been copied. The 40 MB G3 reference array is still not shipped and is documented

verified_in_the_clean_clone: 618 files, 148 MB, nothing unexpectedly ignored by git
pip install -r requirements.txt in an empty venv: numpy 2.2.6, scipy 1.15.3, matplotlib 3.10.9, pandas 2.3.3
all ten tables produce LaTeX identical to the reference environment, byte for byte
all five offline figures rebuild at the published byte sizes
results/toy/figdata.npz rebuilds to the same sha256 as the shipped copy
results/ and assets/ are unchanged by a full run
the scripts also run from a foreign working directory
the README recipe that copies results/summary_json/ into out/summary/ lets the table builders outside scripts/reproduce/ run on the published numbers
left_as_is_by_decision: 58 result JSON files record the absolute Windows paths of the machine the runs were made on. They are provenance inside artefacts whose sha256 is asserted, they carry no user name, and rewriting them would mean editing delivered results. README section 8 says so.
docs/prereg/PREREG_200.md keeps its original wording and language: it is the dated record the sweep was registered against.

stage_d_first_run_experience.what: Every command the README documents was run in a clean export of the repository, in a virtual environment holding only requirements.txt, and the output a first-time user would see was recorded for each one.

found_and_fixed.what: eight entry points answered --help with a ModuleNotFoundError traceback
found_and_fixed.fix: the top-level torch / joblib / scikit-learn import of thirteen modules is wrapped in try/except ModuleNotFoundError, which raises SystemExit naming the package and the README section. No logic changed; only the message when a package is absent.

found_and_fixed.what: the earlier translation pass matched CJK ideographs only, so full-width punctuation survived in 19 modules, and at several seams the English sentence had been truncated, duplicated ('FAIL -- FAIL:', 'v7 recomputed v7') or had lost a space
found_and_fixed.fix: every one of those lines was rewritten against the original wording in the working tree, not guessed. Numbers that the truncation had dropped were restored from the original (for example the A' degeneracy note and the E21 cpu-path tolerances).
found_and_fixed.verified: zero CJK or full-width characters remain outside the frozen, archived and result files; the repository-wide scan now covers U+3000-U+303F, U+4E00-U+9FFF and U+FF00-U+FFEF

found_and_fixed.what: one format string had lost a placeholder in translation, so build_sampler_axis_tables.py would have written the wrong numbers into the A' verdict
found_and_fixed.fix: the three placeholders match .format(ratio, slope, fraction) again; a repository-wide check now confirms every .format() call's placeholder count matches its argument count

found_and_fixed.what: the README promised --help on three scripts that take no arguments, where --help runs the script instead
found_and_fixed.fix: those lines say what the script reads and that it takes no arguments; the README also says how to list all thirteen such scripts

executed_for_real_in_the_clean_clone: the ten table scripts and the five offline figure scripts (fifteen entry points)
scripts/export_classifier_to_numpy.py, on a HistGradientBoostingClassifier fitted here: its own identity gate against predict_proba passed at 1.1e-16 under scikit-learn 1.7.2
fit_selection_classifier.export_portable, the same private-sklearn-API path, on the same classifier: 40 trees, 2388 nodes, identity error 1.1e-16
argument parsing of every other documented entry point

not_executed.what: the training, sampling and scoring numerics
not_executed.why: they need PyTorch, which no package index reachable from this environment serves, and the 1.7 GB of atlas counts plus the fitted discriminators and tilt tables, none of which are redistributed
not_executed.what_was_checked_instead: import resolution, path resolution, argument parsing, and the message each entry point gives when a package or an input is absent
